content.alt: 40. Careful, Careful — Gently! - My child loves the baby, but their hands are so rough
content.text:
My child loves the baby, but their hands are so rough

Your child's heart is brimming with love for the baby, yet when you see them grip too hard while 'hugging' or push while trying to give a kiss, your own heart flutters with worry. It isn't because they mean any harm—it's that they don't yet know how to control their own strength.

When you show them 'how to be gentle' rather than scolding, your child turns clumsy love into tender care.

Curious about the caring-for-baby-sibling storybook? Take a look at its lessons alongside the illustrations. Meet the key scenes of the story too. Read it together with your child and talk it over. From a sibling kindness storybook to a new baby storybook and a kindness storybook, we've gathered many stories around 40. Careful, Careful — Gently!
content.caption: Rough hands aren't ill will—your child is just learning to control their strength.

content.alt: 40. Careful, Careful — Gently! - Why the kindness of controlling your strength matters
content.text:
Why the kindness of controlling your strength matters

The ability to control one's own strength is where kindness begins. A child who knows how to treat someone smaller and weaker gently gets along kindly and safely with friends, too.

What's more, in learning to be 'gentle,' your child also learns what is dangerous. Small habits—putting away sharp things, giving up a turn—become the strength to keep both the baby and themselves safe.
content.caption: The power to treat a small being gently is where kindness begins.

content.alt: 40. Careful, Careful — Gently! - Hori's story of becoming a tender big brother
content.text:
Hori's story of becoming a tender big brother

In 『Careful, Careful — Gently!』, Hori grabs his little sibling's arm too hard while wanting to play, and gets a fright when Hoya nearly cries. Mom shows him the way: "Big brother's hands are big and strong. Careful, careful—gently!"

Hori learns to hug softly 'like a feather, like cotton candy,' and clears away the sharp blocks on the floor. When he stops gripping so hard, Hoya bursts into giggles. Along with Hori, your child learns the feel of 'gentle' and the joy of being kind.
content.caption: He became a tender big brother—hugging gently and clearing away anything dangerous.

content.alt: 40. Careful, Careful — Gently! - Practicing being gentle together at home
content.text:
Practicing being gentle together at home

'Gentle' has to be learned by feel more than by words. Like the book's comparison, try a game of softly pressing palms together 'like a feather, like cotton candy.' Practicing hugging a doll gently, imagining it's the baby, is great too.

When your child treats the baby gently, praise it big: "You hugged so gently, and the baby's smiling!" As you clear away sharp objects together, explain the reason—"Let's put this away, it would hurt if the baby stepped on it"—so they learn kindness and safety at once.
content.caption: Like a feather, like cotton candy—practice the feel of gentle together.

content.text:
Frequently Asked Questions

Q. How can I encourage my child to help care for the baby?

A. Show them how to be soft and gentle—careful, careful—as if it were a game. Give them even a small job and praise it big, and their affection for the baby will grow.

Q. How does a caring-for-baby-sibling storybook help?

A. Watching the main character look after their little sibling with such care, your child feels the pride of being a big brother or sister. A caring-for-baby-sibling storybook warmly nurtures a kind heart.

Q. Is it okay to let my oldest look after the baby?

A. It's best for a parent to watch nearby and give small roles within safe limits. When you thank them for helping well, both responsibility and pride grow together.
